title: One week to go!! Prizes and recognition for each track: MVA Hackathon 2026

latest.raw:
Thank you to everyone taking part. With submissions closing on **October 24 at 23:59 UTC**, here is how prizes and recognition work across the two tracks.

**Track 1 (Variant Prediction)**
Track 1 is the _foundational_ track. Its leaderboard is a validation benchmark: it shows whether a pipeline can recover the clinically confirmed answer from real patient data. _Track 1 does not have ranked prizes_. Because nearly every Track 1 team recovered the confirmed answer, a ranked leaderboard prize would not distinguish between them, so we are recognizing all perfect-score teams through *authorship* instead: every team whose best submission earns the full 100 rank points on the final leaderboard will be included as **consortium authors** on the hackathon summary paper. Track 1 submissions are also eligible for the Innovation Prize.

Identifying the causal variant(s) is the starting point for understanding the biological mechanism, which is what Track 2 asks teams to characterize. Teams are encouraged to build on their Track 1 work in a Track 2 submission.

**Track 2 (Drug Repurposing)**
1st, 2nd and 3rd place are selected by the expert panel using the four weighted criteria on the Overview page. Winning teams will also be invited as **named authors** on the hackathon summary paper.

🥇 1st Place: $12,000 cash + $12,000 in Claude credits
🥈 2nd Place: $7,000 cash + $7,000 in Claude credits
🥉 3rd Place: $4,000 cash + $4,000 in Claude credits

**Innovation Prize ($2,000 cash + $2,000 in Claude credits)**
Open to any submission in _either_ track, independent of overall placement, recognizing creativity, community impact or patient-centered design, as described in the Official Rules. The winning team will also be invited as named authors on the hackathon summary paper.

**Publishing your own methods**
Beyond the summary paper, we encourage all teams to share their methods more widely. We are exploring publication options for participants, for example a dedicated collection in an open-access journal such as F1000Research, or preprints on servers such as Research Square, and will share details after the hackathon closes. Your submitted code, write-ups and reports are already released under CC BY 4.0.

**Prize eligibility and payment**
Prizes are subject to eligibility and payment requirements. As set out in rules, **all participants must delete the hackathon data within 30 days of the submission deadline (by November 23) and confirm this by email to cnb@sagebase.org**. Prizes, including cash and Claude credits, are released once this confirmation is received and any required tax documentation and sanctions screening are complete.

**Timeline**
Submissions close October 24 at 23:59 UTC. Winners will be announced on December 18.
